_description: Cash interest must enter the STATE ordinary tax base, not just the federal one. Single filer in Illinois (flat 4.95%, no state standard deduction) whose only taxable income is $10k of cash-account interest. Regression guard for the bug where computeStateTax received the pre-interest otherTaxableGross while the federal path used the interest-inclusive value.
_rationale: Cash $250k @ 4% yield -> cashInterest = $10,000 (credited on beginning-of-year balance). Cash interest is ordinary income (not retirement income, so no state retirement exclusion applies; not a Traditional withdrawal). No wage/pension income, no brokerage, no SS -> the $10k interest is the ONLY ordinary income. FEDERAL: combined taxable = $10,000; 2026 single standard deduction $16,100 -> federal taxable = max(0, 10000 - 16100) = 0 -> federal ordinary tax = $0. STATE (Illinois): flat 4.95%, standardDeduction null -> $0 deduction; state ordinary base = ordinaryGross($10,000) + 0 + 0 = $10,000 -> state ordinary tax = 0.0495 x 10000 = $495.00. ordinaryTax = $0 federal + $495 state = $495. No LTCG (no brokerage), NIIT disabled (and MAGI $10k << $200k anyway), IRMAA disabled (age 60, pre-Medicare) -> totalTax = $495. BEFORE THE FIX the state path saw $0 of interest -> stateOrdinaryTax $0 -> ordinaryTax/totalTax would have been $0, so these checks fail pre-fix and pass post-fix. Age 60 -> 63 (4 years) with $250k cash vs ~$30.5k/yr need -> always solvent -> 100%.
name: State Cash Interest Ordinary
